title: Can an odd number plus an even number be a multiple of six?
description: Seven plus eight and nine plus twelve are tried first, then an even number is written as two n and an odd number as two m plus one. Their sum is one more than an even number, so it is odd, and every multiple of six is even. Keeko raises the doubt that twenty one is a multiple of three, so it is a multiple of six.
teaching_notes: One idea: an even number plus an odd number is one more than an even number, so it is odd, and a multiple of six is always even. Watch for students who test two examples and stop, or who think every multiple of three is a multiple of six.

source: Try 7 + 8 and 9 + 12, then explain with algebra why an odd n
video_script.why: A learner tries two examples, writes an even and an odd number with letters, and explains why their sum can never be a multiple of six.
video_script.substitution: the book's own sums: seven plus eight, and nine plus twelve
video_script.anchor: pairs of dots with one single dot left over, as in the book
video_script.wrong_answer: twenty one is a multiple of three so it is a multiple of six
video_script.wrong_move: thinks a multiple of three must be a multiple of six, forgetting that a multiple of six must be even
video_script.payoff_line: An odd number plus an even number is never a multiple of six. The sum is odd, and every multiple of six is even.

final_answer.value: Never true: odd plus even is odd, and every multiple of 6 is even
final_answer.spoken: an odd number plus an even number is never a multiple of six, because the sum is odd and every multiple of six is even

hold_back: Never true: odd plus even is odd, and every multiple of 6 is even
maths_rules: 7 + 8 = 15 and 9 + 12 = 21: both odd, neither a multiple of 6
even number = 2n, odd number = 2m + 1; sum = 2n + 2m + 1 = 2(n + m) + 1, one more than an even number, so odd
multiple of 6 = 6j = 2 x 3j, even; an odd number cannot equal an even number
doubt: 21 = 3 x 7 is a multiple of 3; 6 x 3 = 18 and 21 - 18 = 3 left over, and 21 is odd
video_script.design: One idea: odd plus even is odd, and a multiple of six is even. Assumes the forms two n and two m plus one. Wrong idea: a multiple of three is a multiple of six. Pairs of dots stay on the board with one single dot set apart.

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, try the examples. Seven plus eight is fifteen, which is odd.

narration: <bookmark mark='even'/>Step two, use letters. Write the even number as two n, which is n pairs.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>Write the odd number as two m plus one, which is m pairs and one single.

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add them. Two n plus two m plus one is two times the bracket n plus m, plus one.
<bookmark mark='single'/>That is one more than an even number, so the sum is odd.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>An odd number plus an even number is never a multiple of six. The sum is odd, and every multiple of six is even.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks twenty one is a multiple of three so it is a multiple of six.
<bookmark mark='left'/>But six times three is eighteen, and three are left over.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A multiple of six must be even, and twenty one is odd.
